history.period: Idol Pala era (c. 8th-12th century); temple built c. 1922
history.summary: A historic Vaishnava shrine at Asuran Chowk on Medical College Road. Its four-armed black-stone idol of Vishnu is attributed to the Pala dynasty (8th-12th century). Found in 1914 by a mason named Gorakh, the idol passed to the Lucknow Museum; after a campaign led by Queen Shyam Sundari Kumari of Majhauli state (who commissioned the temple in memory of her husband King Kaushal Kishore Prasad Mall), the court returned it and the idol was installed on 8 May 1922. The elevated white-stone complex includes shrines representing the four dhams (Jagannath Puri, Badrinath, Rameshwaram, Dwarka). Note: coordinates are for Asuran Chowk (street-level match), not the temple's exact point - verify. Opening hours unverified.

town_description: Gorakhpur is a major city in eastern Uttar Pradesh (Purvanchal), on the Rapti river, named after Yogi Gorakhnath. It is a cultural and religious hub with Gorakhnath Math as its best-known shrine, and a rail and road gateway to Nepal and the Terai.
